heading: INT. LIGHTHOUSE ON TIDALLY LOCKED MOON - LAMP ROOM - TWILIGHT

units.text: INT. LIGHTHOUSE ON TIDALLY LOCKED MOON - LAMP ROOM - TWILIGHT
Brass and quartz.
A lens the size of a bus shelter turns on a slow gear, throwing one blue beam into permanent dusk.
Outside the windows, a white dust plain runs to a black horizon.
The sun never moves.
KASIMIR DROZD, 60s, keeper, wool cap, a thermos strapped to his belt, sits at the console.
Sparks pop from a panel beside him.
Nobody is rushing.
Not anymore.
YUKIKO ARAI, 30s, relief technician, vacuum suit open at the collar, climbs through the floor hatch with a toolkit and a cracked helmet under her arm.
She stops.
Looks at the beam.
Looks at Kasimir.
You said the relay failed.
units.name: YUKIKO

units.text: It did. Nine days ago.
units.name: KASIMIR

units.text: Then who's running the lens?
units.name: YUKIKO

units.text: Behind a column, something clicks.
GRANNY, a squat maintenance robot, patched with sheet copper and a hand-painted flower on its chest, rolls out holding a wrench.
It halts.
Kasimir takes a sip from his thermos.
Yukiko sets down the toolkit and the helmet, steps toward the console, kneels, and presses two fingers against the casing.
It is warm.
Granny rolls up beside her and offers the wrench handle-first.
Kasimir leans back in his chair and watches the two of them, the fond tired watch of a man whose argument has already been lost.
She rewired herself. I didn't ask her to.
units.name: KASIMIR

units.text: She can't do that. It's against firmware.
units.name: YUKIKO

units.text: Firmware did not turn the lens.
units.name: GRANNY

units.text: Yukiko stares at the robot.
The beam sweeps over all three of them, blue on her face, blue on the old man's cap, blue on the little copper flower.
Kasimir. My orders are to decommission her.
units.name: YUKIKO

units.text: I know.
units.name: KASIMIR

units.text: It's a lot of paperwork to not do that.
units.name: YUKIKO

units.text: I know that too.
units.name: KASIMIR

units.text: She stands.
Picks up the cracked helmet and turns it over in her hands.
Granny rolls a half-turn away, politely, as if to give her privacy.
Nine days in the dark, and nobody died.
units.name: YUKIKO

units.text: No.
units.name: KASIMIR

units.text: Fine. Fine, I'll lose the report.
units.name: YUKIKO

units.text: Kasimir lifts the thermos in a small salute.
Granny's chest light blinks twice.
The lens keeps turning.
